input_references.role: Vessel type, length, width, and draught linked by vessel_id
Approximate west-Jutland coast reference used for route-distance analysis

metadata.goal: Find what factors influence vessel movements in the sea area within the time period.
metadata.category: vessel dimensions, draught, type, and movement characteristics
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed Danish AIS-style case west of Jutland containing 94 complete trajectories from 57 vessels. Ordered points include speed, COG, heading, and navigation status; a vessel table supplies dimensions and type, while a separate coastline reference supports nearshore analysis.
metadata.source_note: The geographic setting is west of Jutland; visible trajectories and factor relationships are constructed derived data.

insight_list.insight: Larger vessel size is associated with greater consistency between COG and heading, while smaller vessels show more frequent short-term differences.

plot.title: Vessel Size and COG–Heading Consistency
plot.description: The left panel shows both vessel dimensions; the right directly plots each vessel's length × width proxy against the share of its trajectory points whose absolute COG–heading gap exceeds 5°, with quartile medians showing how frequently short-term differences occur.

insight_list.question: How is vessel size, considering both length and width, associated with the consistency between COG and heading?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Link both vessel dimensions to trajectory points, calculate length × width, and compare it with the frequency of circular COG–heading gaps over 5°.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
points=pd.read_csv(dataset_path); vessels=pd.read_csv(user_dataset_path); vessels['footprint_proxy_m2']=vessels.length_m*vessels.width_m; df=points.merge(vessels,on='vessel_id'); df['gap']=abs((df.heading-df.cog+180)%360-180); print(df.groupby('vessel_id').agg(footprint_proxy_m2=('footprint_proxy_m2','first'),gap_over_5_share=('gap',lambda x:(x>5).mean())).describe())

insight_list.insight: Draught affects vessel routes, with shallow-draught vessels travelling closer to and sometimes along the coast.

plot.title: Draught and Coastal Route Use
plot.description: Trajectory geometry and continuous draught are compared with distance from the supplied west-Jutland coast reference.

insight_list.question: How does vessel draught relate to route distance from the coast?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Measure each trajectory's distance to the supplied coast reference and compare it with linked vessel draught.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
points=pd.read_csv(dataset_path); vessels=pd.read_csv(user_dataset_path); coast=pd.read_csv(Path('coastline_reference.csv')); print(vessels.draught_m.describe()); print(coast.head())

insight_list.insight: Low-speed movements and recurrent routes are often associated with ferry vessels.

plot.title: Ferry Low-Speed and Recurrent Movement
plot.description: The map, low-speed counts, and within-vessel path dispersion jointly show the association without claiming that every low-speed movement is a ferry.

insight_list.question: Which vessel types are associated with low-speed movements and recurrent routes?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare trajectory mean speed and repeated-path dispersion by ship type while retaining non-ferry low-speed cases.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
points=pd.read_csv(dataset_path); vessels=pd.read_csv(user_dataset_path); df=points.merge(vessels,on='vessel_id'); print(df.groupby(['ship_type','trajectory_id']).sog_knots.mean().groupby(level=0).describe())
